title: [News] CPU Price Hike Wave: Intel Reportedly Up to 20%, Qualcomm 10%, AMD May Join as TSMC Costs Climb
source_used: TrendForce News (fulltext from main session), relaying Commercial Times and Central News Agency
key_facts: Commercial Times: Intel and Qualcomm have raised prices for certain processors; AMD is reportedly preparing adjustments (size, scope and timing unconfirmed).

Intel has raised processor prices three times since late last year; price adjustments across product lines reportedly began 1 Sep, with high-end Panther Lake models up 15% to 20% and Meteor Lake and Arrow Lake up 5% to 10%.
Qualcomm raised prices on PC processor platforms including Snapdragon X and X2 Elite by about 10% from October, citing supply-chain sources.

Central News Agency: analysts expect TSMC to raise prices in 2027 by 5% to 10% for advanced nodes, 10% to 15% for advanced packaging and 3% to 5% for mature nodes, on higher raw material and equipment costs.

AMD has begun ramping its sixth-generation EPYC 'Venice' on TSMC's 2nm; Reuters reported CEO Lisa Su said on 6 Oct that AMD is working with TSMC and others to expand CPU and GPU capacity for AI demand.

TrendForce: rising DRAM and SSD prices plus higher CPU costs add pressure on notebook makers, though CPU supply has improved since 2Q26 and the 2026 notebook shipment decline is expected to narrow to 9.4% year on year.
quote_evidence: According to Commercial Times, Intel and Qualcomm have raised prices for certain processor products, while AMD is reportedly preparing adjustments of its own.
Qualcomm has also moved to raise chip prices.
However, continued increases in DRAM and SSD prices, alongside higher CPU costs, are putting further pressure on notebook makers.
why_it_matters_hint: Higher chip prices can feed into dearer laptops and PCs, but the increases come from Taiwanese press reports and supply-chain sources, not company announcements.
event_date: Intel adjustments reportedly from 1 Sep 2026; Qualcomm from Oct 2026; reported 12 Oct 2026
notes: Read in full from the fulltext copy. Chain: Commercial Times is the first reporter for the Intel, Qualcomm and AMD claims; Central News Agency for the TSMC forecast; TrendForce relays both. Not carried in earlier editions of the last 14 days.
